text:
alex: Heads up — cross-account lambda started getting AccessDenied when calling KMS decrypt (envelope) a few mins ago. Error in app logs: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::222222222:assumed-role/ingest-lambda-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111:key/abcd-1234` Anyone seen this pattern? @maria

maria: Can you paste the key policy + the assume-role trust policy? Also cloudtrail decrypt event id if you have it.

alex: CloudTrail event: `eventID: 4a3b2c-9d8e-...` I'll paste the key policy we have. Note: key is in acct 111111111, caller is acct 222222222.
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid":"AllowAccountRoot","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111111111:root"},"Action":"kms:*","Resource":"*"},
    {"Sid":"AllowEncrypt","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/encryptor"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```

sam: Looks like nothing explicitly allows the external account. Cross-account decrypt needs either key policy Principal matching the caller ARN or a grant. Do we use grants for this flow?

alex: We used grants previously but recent rotation might've removed the grants. I don't see any active Grants in KMS console for that key.

tia: If you're using assumed role from acct 222, key policy must mention `arn:aws:iam::222222222:root` or the specific role, or the IAM principal in acct 111 must have a policy and there's a grant. Also STS session tags can block via IAM session policy. Did we add a session policy on assume-role?

ryan: CloudTrail shows assumeRole call with sessionPolicy present: `SessionPolicy: {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Action":"kms:*","Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:EncryptionContext:source":"restricted"}}}]}` — that would block kms:Decrypt if encryption context matched.

maria: Ah, that explains it. The key policy only allowed `arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/encryptor` but not the assumed role. We have two options: add the external role to key policy, or create a KMS Grant scoped to the external principal. I prefer grant since it's easier to rotate.

alex: @sam can you create a grant for `arn:aws:sts::222222222:assumed-role/ingest-lambda-role/*` with `kms:Decrypt,kms:GenerateDataKey` scoped to the CMK? Add an encryptionContext restriction to match `task=ingest`.

sam: On it. Creating grant now. Quick Q: grants don't survive key rotation if you re-create key; they are tied to CMK. We're rotating by schedule (alias points to new key). Confirming they want grant on each new CMK.

alex: Yes, need docs update. Also we should fix the assume-role session policy — remove the Deny or limit context earlier. For now gift grant will unblock.

ops-bot: grant created: GrantId: 9f2a7c1d-... by sam — applies to key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111:key/abcd-1234 — expires: 2024-10-01T12:00:00Z

tia: After grant applied, can someone trigger decrypt test? Use `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob` with `--profile crossacct`

alex: Re-tested — decrypt succeeded. Thanks. Follow-ups: add an automation to recreate grants after key rotation and add monitoring alert if Decrypt AccessDenied spikes. Filing a ticket.

ryan: Opened ticket #INFRA-492: automate-grant-recreate-on-rotation — assign infra team.

maria: :thumbsup: Good catch on session policy. We should also add log-based alert on `kms:Decrypt AccessDenied` in CloudWatch/Datadog.
